source_message.text:
Yes, that's correct. The main board has:

\- ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 module
\- INA219 current monitor (on the 3.3V rail)
\- USB-C connector (programming port) + LDO for standalone operation
\- All the JST connectors (to power board, sensor board, display, PIR, touch, LEDs, buttons, reset)
\- Support passives: decoupling caps, pull-ups, series resistors, Schottky diodes, BOOT button

No sensors, no power management — those are on the other boards.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Dusko,

USB is fully working after the rework (U3 removed, data lines
bridged), boards enumerate and flash fine. Here is how the power and
AXP2101 behave after that, tested on both boards with identical
results:

1\. DCDC1 idles at 3.16V. The register is confirmed 3.3V (0x82 reads
0x12), so the converter regulates 4 percent low.
2\. Any load transient collapses the rail: SPI flash erase (about
150mA step) or WiFi TX burst (300-400mA) drops the 3.3V below
2.5V and hard resets the ESP32. Brown-out detector disabled makes
no difference, it is a true rail collapse. Adding 330uF external
capacitance does not help. The board cannot run standalone on USB.
3\. It works when powered from battery only (VSYS around 3.8V), but
fails on 5V USB input. So it fails exactly when the buck actually
has to regulate, and survives near dropout.
4\. Writing DCDC1 to 3.4V over I2C helps a lot: boot, WiFi serving and
a full 1.9MB OTA write all pass. But the WiFi calibration surge at
reboot still collapses it. Also strange: the 0x82 write was
ignored on several boots (readback stayed 0x12) and then latched
on a later boot. Other register writes verify fine, and the VBUS
input current limit default is 1.5A, so it is not input limiting.
5\. I replaced L3 with a larger 2.2uH inductor with much higher
saturation current. No change at all. The inductor is not the
problem, the original DFE252010F spec was fine anyway.
6\. During further testing, DCDC1 on board 2 degraded progressively
and finally died: its output now measures about 265 ohm to GND
with everything disconnected, so the output stage is leaking.
7\. With an external 3.3V feed the whole board works perfectly for
hours: boot, PSRAM, e-paper, WiFi, web UI, sensors. Everything
downstream is healthy.

My conclusion: the AXP2101 chips themselves are suspect (bad batch,
counterfeit, moisture damage at reflow, or parts with non-standard
factory programming). I asked the factory for the sourcing and lot
codes. One thing worth checking on your side: the local input
decoupling on the DCDC1 VIN pins in the layout, whether there is a
capacitor close to the pin or only the bulk group further away.

Do you see any other explanation that fits all of this? Hi Dusko,
